instruction: As a wire-EDM CNC programming expert, explain the following programming practice.
input: Adaptive control M90 only on rough pass — disable M91 for skims
output: On the Mitsubishi FA-10S at JM Die, Adaptive Control (M90 = on, M91 = off) is used ONLY during the rough cut (Pass 1). The program structure observed in all production programs: M91 (disable AC) is called at program start before threading, M90 (enable AC) is called immediately after the Pass 1 E-code, and subsequent skim passes run without any M90/M91 call — meaning they inherit M91 (off) state. Adaptive control during skimming introduces servo hunting because the low power skim discharge looks like a near-short to the AC algorithm. Running skims with AC on degrades Ra by 10-15% and causes dimensional scatter. Always structure programs: M91 → thread → M90 with E-code Pass 1 → (skims run without M90).

instruction: As a wire-EDM CNC programming expert, explain the following programming practice.
input: Makino EPAC code pattern: roughing uses 10x6 series (1006/1016/1026), finish uses 150x series
output: Makino DUO EPAC code naming: roughing passes use 10X6 pattern where X indicates thickness range (0=1mm, 1=3mm, 2=5mm, 3=10mm). Finish passes use E150X + E150(X+1) progression. Each EPAC contains complete pulse parameters.

instruction: Advise on wire-EDM material handling for the following.
input: Plain brass wire — tensile strength governs taper vs threading tradeoff (400-900 N/mm²)
output: Bedra Bercocut plain brass wire (CuZn37) ships in tensile strengths 400-900 N/mm². The low end (400 N/mm², soft / >30% elongation) is the only viable choice for extreme taper cuts to 45° because high-elongation wire bends without snapping, but it threads unreliably and is unusable on automated lights-out production. The hard end (900 N/mm², <2% elongation) is the workhorse for >80% of WEDM jobs: threads first-try every time on AWT, runs all-night unattended, but caps taper at ~15°. Wires with low elongation will thread reliably but are limited in tapering ability; conversely, wires with high elongation can taper-cut to 45° but with much reduced threading reliability. Industry US/EU Cu/Zn alloy ratio is 63/37; Asian convention is 65/35. Tensile range across all alloys is 54-173 ksi (370-1190 N/mm²) — pick the lowest tensile that still threads on your AWT.

instruction: Advise on the wire-EDM machining practice below.
input: Glue stop M01 between closed contours: JM Die slug control practice
output: When a program contains multiple closed contour cutouts (e.g., a die insert with two punch holes), JM Die inserts an M01 (Optional Stop / Glue Stop) block after the rough pass of each contour closes but BEFORE the skim passes begin. The typical sequence is: rough contour 1 → G40 lead-out → M01 (Glue Stop) → M78 M78 → skims for contour 1. The M01 gives the operator a pause to apply a dab of cyanoacrylate adhesive to hold the slug, then press cycle start to continue with skim passes. Without this stop, heavy slugs can drop mid-skim and jam the lower guide or shift the work. The comment '(Glue Stop)' is the standard JM Die in-program annotation — use it consistently so operators recognize it.

instruction: Advise on wire-EDM quality / surface integrity for the following.
input: Recast layer thickness determines part integrity
output: WEDM always leaves a recast (white) layer on the cut surface. Thickness: rough cut 15-25µm, after 2 skims 5-10µm, after 4 skims 1-3µm. For aerospace (AMS 2628) and medical parts, maximum recast is typically 7.5µm (0.0003in). If recast exceeds spec after WEDM, mechanical polishing or chemical etching is required. Thermal penetration depth follows Carslaw-Jaeger: d = 2×sqrt(α×t_on). Lower ON time = thinner recast.

instruction: Advise on wire-EDM speeds/feeds for the situation below.
output: For workpiece thickness >100mm, increase gap voltage by 5-10V above the standard setting. The longer spark gap path through the dielectric has higher electrical resistance, requiring more voltage to maintain stable discharge. Without compensation, the discharge frequency drops and cutting speed decreases more than expected. Mitsubishi FA machines have automatic thickness compensation — enable it via the SV (servo voltage) parameter.

instruction: Advise on the wire-EDM machining practice below.
input: JM Die M2 high-speed steel — aggressive roughing OK, add skim for surface hardness
output: M2 high-speed steel (0.85%C, 4%Cr, 5%Mo, 6%W, 2%V) at 60-65 HRC is used at JM Die for forming punches and extrusion tooling. Despite high hardness, M2 cuts well on wire EDM due to good electrical conductivity from tungsten/molybdenum carbides. On FA-20S: E12xx standard at full power (100%), no derating needed. However, M2's surface hardness is affected by EDM recast — the recast layer loses the secondary hardening from carbide precipitation. Always use 4+ skim passes on M2 to fully remove recast layer. After wire EDM, M2 parts often receive a light temper (400-450°F for 1 hour) to restore surface hardness.

instruction: Advise on wire-EDM speeds/feeds for the situation below.
input: Material affects achievable Ra: hardened steel is better than aluminum
output: Counter-intuitively, hardened tool steels (D2, A2, S7 at 58-62 HRC) produce BETTER surface finish in WEDM than soft materials like aluminum 6061. Reason: hard materials produce smaller, more uniform discharge craters. Typical achievable Ra after 4 skim passes: D2 hardened=0.15µm, 304SS=0.25µm, 6061 Al=0.4µm, WC=0.10µm. Klocke (2013) attributes this to the higher melting point and lower thermal conductivity concentrating discharge energy into smaller craters.

instruction: Provide wire-EDM safety guidance for the following.
input: Counterfactual safe_mode reduces wire breakage by 55% for thick sections (>80mm)
output: Counterfactual analysis shows that applying 'safe_mode' parameters (increased Toff, reduced wire tension, lower feed) reduces wire breakage by 55% for workpiece thickness exceeding 80mm. Trade-off is 28% longer cycle time.

instruction: Advise on the wire-EDM machining practice below.
input: JM Die D2 tool steel parameters — optimal for cold heading die cavities
output: D2 tool steel (1.55%C, 12%Cr, 0.85%Mo) is JM Die's primary material for cold heading die cavities. Wire EDM characteristics: high hardness at 58-62 HRC, excellent wear resistance, but tendency to micro-crack if heat-affected zone (HAZ) is excessive. For D2 on the FA-20S: use E12xx standard at 80% power (reduce from default 100%), increase OFF time by 10% to reduce HAZ, and always run at least 3 skim passes to remove recast layer. Expected cutting rate: 1.8-2.2 in²/hr on 1" stock. Never skip final skim on D2 — the recast layer contains carbide precipitates that accelerate punch wear if left in place.

instruction: Advise on the wire-EDM machining practice below.
input: UV taper only on G1 lines — G2/G3 arcs are straight
output: In standard WEDM taper programming, UV offset (taper) applies ONLY to G1 (linear) moves. G2/G3 arc moves are cut with UV=0 (straight). This is the correct behavior — a tapered arc would require 5-axis simultaneous interpolation that most WEDM machines cannot do. If the part requires tapered arcs, approximate them with short G1 segments (0.1-0.5mm chord) with linear UV interpolation. The NOZE TEST program demonstrates this: UV appears only on G1 blocks.

instruction: Advise on wire-EDM material handling for the following.
input: Zinc-coated wire cuts 20% faster than plain brass at 19% IACS conductivity
output: Zinc-coated EDM wires (Bedra Cobracut / Megacut / AC Cut G) apply a 2-3 µm electro-galvanized pure-zinc layer onto a CuZn36 brass core. Conductivity drops to 19-22% IACS (vs 100% IACS for the original copper-wire EDM electrode), but cutting speed INCREASES 20% over plain brass — the zinc layer vaporizes preferentially, creating a more aggressive plasma channel without the wire breaking. Bedra AC Cut G is specifically rated for AgieCharmilles machines with IPG-or-earlier generators and achieves the +20% speed gain. Pure zinc coatings appear shiny silver; zinc-oxide coatings appear dull gray and trade some speed for better wire-break-resistance against carbides and PCD. Wire tensile strength range for zinc-coated: 61-130 ksi (420-900 N/mm²). Recommended path: roughing on Cobracut Type G (900 N/mm², hard, wear-resistant); finishing on Cobracut Type A standard (500 N/mm², softer, better surface finish).

instruction: Share the JM Die shop-floor wire-EDM practice for the following.
input: JM Die WEDM archive scale — 4,058 files / 100 customer folders / 22 NC programs / ~4,000 Mastercam .mcx-8 projects
output: Empirical scale of the JM Die WIRE EDM archive at H:/PRISM/JM DIE/WIRE EDM/ (analyzed 2026-04-14, codified in jm-die-wedm-program-patterns.ts JM_DIE_WEDM_PROGRAM_ANALYSIS): 4,058 total files across 100 customer folders. The 22 NC/MIN raw G-code programs are the ground truth for FA-10S behavior; the ~4,000 .mcx-8 files are Mastercam X8 project sources that emitted those NC files via the JM Die FA-Series TECH post. Average pass count across analyzed programs = 4.25, max = 5, min = 1. 25% of programs use UV taper (E28xx); 75% use the H175 master-offset convention (the other 25% are taper programs that bypass H175). Most common E-code family: E12xx_standard_4pass. The archive scale matters for two operational reasons: (a) any wizard / AI feature must scale to retrieve / index 4k+ files (.mcx-8 is binary — needs Mastercam to parse, so retrieval-by-customer beats retrieval-by-file-content), (b) only ~0.5% of the archive is human-readable NC source — the remaining 99.5% needs Mastercam round-trip to extract patterns.

instruction: Advise on the wire-EDM machining practice below.
input: JM Die ITW SHAKEPROOF pattern — standard 4-pass for fastener tooling
output: ITW SHAKEPROOF is a high-volume JM Die customer producing fastener heading tooling. Standard program pattern: 4-pass E1221-E1224, H175 master offset at 0.0089", H1-H4 cascade (0.0085/0.0068/0.0059/0.0054), M90 adaptive on rough/first skim. Typical part: punch profile, 0.75-1.5" D2 steel, ±0.0005" tolerance, Ra 20 µin. This pattern achieves 95% quality score and serves as the benchmark for standard punch work. When AI optimizes an amateur program, it should converge toward this pattern for similar part/material combinations.

instruction: Give the JM Die FA-10S shop-calibrated settings for one pass of a wire-EDM cut.
input: Family: 4-axis UV taper, 5-pass — stainless/taper die pattern. Pass 2 of 5 (skim).
output: Pass 2 (skim): E-code E2822, feed 0.23 ipm (5.84 mm/min), H2 wire offset 0 in (0 mm). Skim pass — adaptive control M91 (off); reduce flush pressure vs the rough pass.

instruction: Select the JM Die Mitsubishi FA-10S E-code family for the wire-EDM job described, and say why.
output: Use family E28xx_taper_5pass — 4-axis UV taper, 5-pass — stainless/taper die pattern (5 passes, 4-axis).

instruction: Recommend a wire-EDM wire for the application below and give its key operating specs.
input: Application: Fine features with high speed, Precision finishing (material family: zinc_coated_brass).
output: Bedra Berkenhoff BEDRA TOPAS PLUS — zinc_coated_brass, diameter 0.2 mm, operating tension 10 N (break threshold 16 N), conductivity 22 %IACS, ~$0.06/m. Best for: Fine features with high speed, Precision finishing.
